entities.summary:
The Zanj Rebellion was a massive slave uprising that took place in the 9th century. It occurred in the region of Ahvaz, in what is now modern-day Iran, between 869 and 883 CE. The revolt was sparked by the harsh treatment of slaves by their Arab masters and the desire for freedom and better working conditions.

The Zanj Rebellion was a significant event in the history of the Abbasid Caliphate and had far-reaching consequences. It led to the eventual decline of the Caliphate and the rise of new regional powers. The rebellion also had a profound impact on the social and economic structures of the region, leading to changes in the way slaves were treated and the rise of new forms of labor.

One of the most notable legacies of the Zanj Rebellion is the way it highlighted the deep-seated social and economic problems of the time. The rebellion showed that the system of slavery was not only oppressive but also unsustainable, and it paved the way for future slave rebellions and revolts. As the historian Ibn Battuta noted, 'The Zanj Rebellion was a turning point in the history of the Islamic world, marking the beginning of the end of the Abbasid Caliphate and the rise of new regional powers.'

The Zanj Rebellion also had a lasting impact on the geography of the region. The rebellion helped to create a new power vacuum in the region, which was eventually filled by the Buyid dynasty. This marked the beginning of a new era of regional powers and the decline of the Abbasid Caliphate.

In the end, the Zanj Rebellion was a pivotal moment in the history of the Islamic world. It highlighted the deep-seated social and economic problems of the time and paved the way for future slave rebellions and revolts. As the historian Ibn Battuta noted, 'The Zanj Rebellion was a turning point in the history of the Islamic world, marking the beginning of the end of the Abbasid Caliphate and the rise of new regional powers.'
